publisher: Ministry of Jal Shakti, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (reply in Lok Sabha)
title: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 504, answered 22.07.2021: Pure Drinking Water for All (Annex: State/ UT-wise status of tap water connections in rural households, as on 19.07.2021)
licence: Government of India publication (Lok Sabha answer); reuse with attribution to the source
method: administrative data reported by states to the ministry; measures delivery, not use
coverage: States/UTs and All-India, rural households, JJM-IMIS
limitations: Share of rural households with a household tap connection as reported by States/UTs on JJM-IMIS; it counts connections provided, not whether water flows regularly or is safe (the Ministry's own Functionality Assessment 2024 found 76% of tap connections functional). The denominator (total rural households) is revised by the States over time (e.g. Bihar 197.57 lakh in Feb 2021, 183.54 lakh in Jul 2021-Jul 2022, 166-168 lakh from 2023), so a state's percentage can fall when its household count rises. Delhi and Chandigarh have no rural households in JJM and are not reported.

publisher: Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation (reply in Lok Sabha)
title: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1526, answered 24.11.2016: Review of SBM-G (Annexure-1: State/UT-wise Sanitation Coverage and ODF Villages)
licence: Government of India publication (Lok Sabha answer); reuse with attribution to the source
method: administrative data reported by states to the ministry; measures delivery, not use
coverage: States/UTs and All-India, rural households, SBM(G) MIS
limitations: Coverage of rural households with an individual household latrine as reported by States/UTs on the SBM(G) MIS against the SBM(G) baseline household list; it counts toilets built, not their use. The baseline was revised: answers in 2015-2016 give national coverage on 2.10.2014 as 42.01%, answers from July 2017 as 38.67-38.7%, so 2017 onwards is on a different denominator (break_before=1 on 2017-07-24). Some printed values exceed 100. Jammu & Kashmir includes Ladakh. Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu were separate UTs and are not combined here.
